```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)


dataDir <- "data"
figDir <- "figure"

recodeMissing <- function(x, missCode = 99) {
  ifelse(x == missCode, NA, x)
}

rawData <- read.csv(here("data", "icosw3e02_0.csv"))

# Select relevant variables and transform them using a pipeline
cleanData <- rawData |>
  select(
    yearsCity = w3livedig,     # Outcome (continuous): years lived in the city
    city      = city,          # Predictor 1 (categorical): Munich or Paris
    bornCntr  = w3brncntr,     # Predictor 2 (categorical): born in country (1 = Yes, 2 = No)
    eduYears  = w3eduyrs,      # Predictor 3 (continuous): years of full-time education
    birthYear = w3yrbrn,       # Year of birth (to be converted to age)
    evalTran  = w3evaltran,    # Predictor 5 (0-10 scale): satisfaction with public transport
    airQual   = w3airqual,     # Predictor 6 (0-10 scale): satisfaction with air quality
    trustMun  = w3trstplt_ic   # Predictor 7 (0-10 scale): trust in municipality/politicians
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Apply custom function across variables where 99 represents a missing value
    across(c(yearsCity, eduYears, evalTran, airQual, trustMun), recodeMissing, missCode = 99),
    # Recode 9999 to NA for year of birth and compute age in 2024
    birthYear = recodeMissing(birthYear, missCode = 9999),
    age       = 2024 - birthYear,
    # Convert categorical predictors into labeled factors
    city      = factor(city),
    bornCntr  = factor(bornCntr, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Yes", "No"))
  ) |>
  select(-birthYear) |>  # Remove raw birth year column
  na.omit()              # Keep complete cases only

# Inspect structure and summary statistics of the cleaned dataset
str(cleanData)
summary(cleanData)



```
